problem_type: Paid generation approval and provider payload identity divergence
symptom: A user can approve one sealed generation plan while ProductionRun reserves budget and records an outbox intent before the provider adapter has built the actual wire request. The submission layer can also synthesize its own Approval and budget authorization without consuming the gate decision that represents the human receipt.
direct_cause: ExecutionContract and multi-shot planHash stop at normalized semantic inputs. GenerationProvider.buildRequest runs only inside submit, after authorization and reservation, and productionGenerationSubmission.prepare creates per-job Approval records and budget entries on demand.
class_root: Nomi has no single immutable authorization envelope at the earliest shared paid-generation boundary. Human approval, ProductionRun gate state, pricing, job identity, Canvas evidence, provider idempotency, and the exact provider wire payload can therefore describe different operations while each local check still passes.
affected_population: Users approving single-shot or multi-shot paid generation through semantic MCP
Users approving run_generation_batch through the embedded Project Agent
Users whose provider adapter normalizes, drops, injects, or changes request fields after approval
Users resuming or reconciling ProductionRuns after a crash
Future Skill, MCP, UI, or TaskCenter projections that consume paid-generation state
entry_points: semantic MCP generation gate request, decision, and start
batch scheduler retries and rework attempts
trial-first plan narrowing and budget-resume requests
budget reserve, durable provider-submit intent, and recovery
internal_only_reason: This invariant is entirely owned by Nomi. Provider documentation cannot decide whether Nomi binds its human receipt, budget ledger, outbox, idempotency key, Canvas target, and exact wire payload to one digest.
invariants: A versioned ProductionGenerationAuthorizationEnvelope is created after Canvas evidence and ExecutionContract normalization but before the human challenge, budget mutation, outbox intent, or provider submission.

The envelope freezes immutable project identity and revision, run and plan version, ordered job set, exact Canvas node/result evidence, per-job contract identity, provider/model/parameters/reference roles, provider idempotency identity, exact provider wire payload hash, currency, per-job ceilings, and batch ceiling.

One canonical authorizationDigest is reused as ProductionGenerationPlan.planHash, ProductionGate.planHash, HumanApproval contractHash/targetHash/pricingSnapshotHash, Approval.planHash, and SubmissionOutboxRequest.planHash.
ExecutionContract.contractHash remains a per-job semantic identity and is never relabeled as the batch authorization digest.
GenerationProvider.buildRequest is pure and deterministic for a sealed request; an unstable or changed wire payload fails before budget reservation, ledger mutation, outbox intent, or submit.
productionGenerationSubmission never creates an Approval or budget authorization. It accepts only the Approval atomically created by the approved ProductionRun gate.

Batch scheduling never raises authorization or writes an authorize ledger entry. A new attempt or any additional spend first creates a fresh digest-bound authorization_required job set and waiting gate.
Trial-first invalidates the unapproved envelope, returns the plan to draft with a higher plan version, and requires provider payload preparation plus a fresh seal and gate before submission.
Host persists only the human approval reference and ProductionRun TaskRef; ProductionRun remains the only owner of jobs, gates, budget, outbox, provider receipt, recovery, and artifacts.
The renderer cannot mint a spend grant or dispatch a local Agent generation queue, and nomi_generate cannot reach a direct provider path.

recurrence.reason: Every paid provider, model, single/multi-shot operation, retry, Host/MCP entry, and future request-normalizing adapter reaches the same missing shared identity boundary.
same_class_scan: Scanned run_generation_batch, nomi_generate, semantic generation gate/start, ExecutionContract, multi-shot planHash, approval receipts, ProductionRun gate.decide, Approval storage, budget ledger, submission outbox, runtime envelope, provider buildRequest/submit, retry/reconcile, TaskRef, and Project Agent coordinator paths.

Repaired the multi-shot plan identity so the sealed authorization digest includes project/run/plan/job, Canvas evidence, pricing ceiling, idempotency, and exact provider wire payload identity instead of only ordered shotId:contractHash values.
Moved deterministic provider request construction before approval and added pre-submit payload reconstruction; a changed payload fails before job, ledger, outbox, or provider side effects.
Removed synthetic Approval and budget authorization from productionGenerationSubmission; the approved run gate atomically creates the only accepted Approval and budget authorization.
Removed scheduler-owned authorization raises and authorize-ledger writes; new attempts and additional spend return to a fresh authorization_required job set and waiting gate.
Trial-first now invalidates the unapproved envelope, increments the plan version, and requires provider payload preparation plus a new seal and approval.

Retired renderer run_generation_batch dispatch, the production.generate-node driver route, and the advertised/routable nomi_generate provider path; the nomi_generate policy tombstone remains fail closed.

Verified archive-only cutover removes hash-matched legacy conversation/session sources from active paths after archival, resumes cleanup after a crash, rejects changed sources, and never rehydrates legacy queue, approval, or Undo state.

prevention.strategy: Create and validate one immutable authorization envelope at the main-owned ProductionRun boundary, make provider request construction a deterministic pre-approval operation with pre-submit hash verification, consume only gate-created Approval/budget facts, and delete the renderer and legacy provider bypasses.

migration: Old Agent conversations, Pi context, receipts, and pending approvals are archive-only and never replayed. After the archive and manifest are verified, hash-matched legacy conversations.json and agent-session.json files are removed from active locations; cleanup resumes after a crash, an already-missing source is complete, and a changed source fails closed without deletion. Existing ProductionRuns without an authorization envelope remain inspectable and reconcilable but cannot make a new paid submission; the user must create and approve a fresh plan. Existing provider_accepted/submission_unknown jobs continue observation or reconciliation without resubmission. Documents, Canvas state, assets, exports, and ProductionRun data remain byte-preserved in their domain stores. No dual-write or legacy generation fallback remains.
residual_risks: Provider credentials and transport headers are intentionally outside the body digest; provider adapters must keep authorization secrets out of buildRequest output.
Existing accepted provider tasks cannot retroactively prove their original wire payload and remain legacy audit evidence.
Packaged MCP/Host paid-generation and crash-window journeys remain part of the Phase 3/4 combined exit.
